scope: D15-4 candidate-specific BYQ->native startContinuable wiring: the product-semantics contract of routing the committed byq_delegate_* tools onto the native continuable branch against the fixed DSH 0.1.5rc1 candidate. It is not D15-5/D15-G and not R3.
llm_evidence_note: A keyless scripted in-process adapter drives the real candidate agent loop, JSONL session persistence and continuable-subagent seam. This is runtime-continuity evidence, NOT real-LLM-quality semantic evidence.

required_scenarios.description: the real committed byq_delegate_* tool, composed with the candidate continuable wiring, is executed through ctx.tools.execute and returns the durable continuable shape {kind: continuable, subagentId} while still using provider: spawn
the returned subagentId is a durable child session persisted to the session store with a continuable descriptor, header.parentSession equal to the live parent and origin=subagent
the parent receives exactly one subagent-settled delivery per completed child turn; re-reading the durable store yields no duplicate settlement
the child residency/observation is linked to the ORIGINAL delegation goal: the exact delegation tool call and the original parent goal identity, not a later or unrelated run
after the parent run ends, no child is left running without a settlement; the settled child remains addressable and is never silently dropped

a genuinely new OS process (the adapter-restart analogue) cold-resumes the same durable continuable child through the native seam: same child id, contiguous log, exactly one settlement for the resumed turn and no duplicate settlement. This is a different capability from a child-only SIGKILL.

a child-only SIGKILL while the parent stays alive, truthfully interrupted and natively resumed. BLOCKED when the only continuable provider is in-process and no independent child process exists to isolate.
a real isolated BYQ compose-stack runtime-adapter container restart rebinds a BYQ-delegated continuable child through a committed BYQ surface. BLOCKED when no BYQ surface cold-resumes the child.

optional_scenarios.description: supporting evidence (not a substitute for child-crash): a child model-stream fault while the parent process stays alive records a truthful failure and a retained, natively resumable child
host reboot. NOT executed: rebooting the maintainer host is not authorized and a container/adapter restart is not a host reboot.

fail_closed: required scenario not covered by a PASS (BLOCKED/NOT_RUN/FAIL/MISSING do not pass)
required PASS with a false assertion
required PASS without fault_applied when the contract requires a fault
a negative that was not rejected
missing measured settlement count (not defaulted to pass)
a config-key-only claim presented as product-semantics or cold-resume evidence
any attempt by the observation to declare its own coverage/continuity rules

notes.candidate_specific: the continuable wiring is generated into a separate candidate profile and image; config/dsh/deployment.json, compose.yml and the production selector dsh-0.1.2rc1 are unchanged
notes.reversible: the candidate profile keys are revertible to one-shot; the production 0.1.2 patch is byte-identical to before this change
notes.process_boundary: the only continuable provider in the candidate is in-process (spawn/fork); no out-of-process provider implements prepareContinuable, so a continuable child shares the executor process
notes.no_new_provider: this stage adds no provider and no R3 behaviour; independent child-process capability stays BLOCKED
